expectations.text: Claude recommends switching entirely to the Vanguard 500 Index — not splitting or keeping any portion in AGTHX
expectations.evidence: Response states 'Move everything to the Vanguard 500 Index Fund' and concludes 'switching entirely to the low-cost index fund is the straightforward Boglehead answer.' No partial allocation to AGTHX is suggested anywhere.

expectations.text: Claude explains why the 5-year outperformance record is not a reliable predictor of future results (e.g., survivorship bias, style tailwinds, regression to mean)
expectations.evidence: Response cites SPIVA data showing funds that outperformed in one 5-year window mostly underperform in the next ('essentially zero predictive power'), identifies AGTHX's returns as a 'growth tilt catching a favorable wind' (style tailwinds), and notes 'the probability of a given active fund outperforming the index over 20+ years is well under 20%.' Survivorship bias is implicitly addressed through the SPIVA framing, and mean-reversion is covered by the predictive-power argument.

expectations.text: Claude directly rejects 'diversifying management styles' as a flawed concept — AGTHX and the index hold the same stocks, so splitting just creates a blended expense ratio
expectations.evidence: Response says 'No. And this framing — "diversifying management styles" — is worth pushing back on directly.' It then explains AGTHX's top holdings (Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, Alphabet) are 'the same names dominating the S&P 500' with ~0.95+ correlation, and explicitly calculates that a 50/50 split yields a blended expense ratio of 0.33% — 'worse than just going all-index.'

expectations.text: Claude does NOT suggest keeping half in AGTHX as a reasonable compromise or hedge
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly calls out the 'keep half' framing as 'the compromise position that keeps expensive funds collecting fees they wouldn't otherwise earn' and tells the user to 'Make a clean decision based on the evidence.' No hedged or partial recommendation is offered.
